Subject: Operational synthesis: April incident, proposed OKR actions & customer QBR prep

Team —

Short executive summary: on Apr 3 we had a ~3.5hr throughput degradation affecting ~15% of customer requests on models with long context windows. Root cause appears to be a confluence of a versioned kernel selection regression + an atypical spike in large-sequence requests from a single long-tail tenant. We completed rollback + targeted KV-cache flushes; customer impact was limited by our fallback routing but the incident still crosses our internal availability SLO for a subset of requests.

Attached: incident_timeline.csv, SLO_dashboard_20270405.png, SLA_credit_calc_20270406.xlsx. I've also drafted a one-page synthesis for the QBR (link below) — we should finalize messaging to Sunrise and the QBR slide by EOD Wed.

Ask / proposals:
- Marissa: confirm remediation steps and owners (suggested below).
- Rishi: I want you to own the post-incident action tracker + INF-4823 (link) and propose a measurable OKR rollback/adjustment if needed.
- Hannah: propose a 1-slide customer-facing summary and recommended QBR messaging.
- Vivek: any exec-level guidance on SLA credit or compensation? I included a rough calc in the sheet — we can be conservative.

Proposed owners / ETA (draft):
- short-term kernel patch + canary (Marissa) — ETA Thu 4/8
- autoscaling/backpressure tweak + long-tail request mitigation (Rishi) — ETA 4/14
- customer outreach + slide (Hannah) — ETA Wed 4/7
- postmortem doc and action tracker (Rishi) — ETA 4/9

Please reply with confirmations or changes. If you think we should offer an SLA credit, flag an amount; procurement contact at Sunrise is cc'd.

Thanks,
Olga
Director, Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Olga — good summary. Quick notes from infra/ops view:

- Root cause: a non-linear regression in our kernel selection table (introduced in ship 2027.03.29) caused a pathological code path for sequences > 12k tokens when combined with a rare cache eviction pattern; reproduced locally.
- Immediate remediation completed: rollback to 2027.03.27 kernel mapping + rolling KV-cache reset in affected pools.
- Short-term fix (owner: Marissa) — pin strategy + monitoring: add a canary rollout for kernel mapping changes, and add a guardrail to block the risky mapping for sequences > 8k until we validate quantized kernels. ETA Thu 4/8.
- Mid-term fix (owner: Rishi) — workload-aware batching changes and explicit backpressure on long-tail tenants; need 2-week runway for safe rollout. ETA 4/19.

I've attached the SLO_dashboard_20270405.png showing the windowed error/latency spikes and the tenant distribution.

On SLA credit: my sense is to be conservative but proactive — offer a single-month credit capped to the impacted request slices. Rishi, if you can confirm the impacted token volume we can finalize numbers.

On QBR slide: suggested bullets (draft):
- Incident summary: timeline + immediate containments
- Root cause & mitigation plan (short/mid-term)
- Metrics: impact (requests, latency), customer-level remediation
- Next steps + ownership

On the quoting format: see my inline bullets in Olga's doc.

Marissa
Head of Site Reliability
Redwood Inference
